relationship_to_rr4.rule: The RR4 amendment remains binding for the historical RR4 debug workstream. It is not edited or retroactively broadened. R28 is a new prospective workstream with new source, preregistration, run ID, and evidence directory.
relationship_to_rr4.historical_evidence_policy: RR4 Attempt C remains scientifically invalid and Debug D remains nonformal two-fault engineering evidence. Neither is pooled with R28 detector outcomes.
known_prior_observations: RR4 Attempt C had nine matched-clean integration aborts and zero semantic sidecars.
RR4 Debug D established live matched-clean logit capture for M8 and M9.
RR4 Debug D observed an experiment sentinel for M8 and a production paired-paged-view assertion for M9.

r28_scope.case_design: For every M1--M9 fault, execute one fresh matched-clean case with all gates enabled and one separately rebuilt mutant case with only its preregistered target gate suppressed.
r28_scope.forkaudit_reference_lane: Use the separately executed, manifest-bound RR2 W-run receipt as the authoritative all-gates-on ForkAudit target-gate observation; do not pool it with R28 as a detection rate.
comparison_detectors: other ForkAudit gate after target suppression
exactly allowlisted M7 or M9 production assertion
r28_scope.unallowlisted_exception_policy: Every exception other than a non-target ForkAudit gate, the exact M8 payload abort, or an exact M7/M9 production assertion is operational invalid and cannot be counted as a detector outcome.
excluded_claims: detector completeness or population detection rate

reporting_policy.incremental_value_claim_condition: An incremental-value statement is authorized only for individually identified faults caught by the separate RR2 ForkAudit lane for which the valid R28 target-suppressed mutant completes without another ForkAudit gate or an allowlisted production assertion and has fully evaluated token and logit comparisons that do not detect the fault.
reporting_policy.forbidden_aggregation: Do not combine separate executions into a probability, detection rate, or false-negative rate.
